name: nds_rtc
statement: The DS real-time clock (Seiko S-35199A01) on three wires through the ARM7's RTC register: chip select, clock and data, each with a direction bit. A transfer is a command byte (fixed code 0110, a register number, a read bit) and the register's bytes, least significant bit first; date and time are BCD. The clock starts from what the host sets (the shell sets the wall clock; tests set a fixed date) and runs on machine time.

registers.name: RTC
registers.bits: 0 data, 1 clock, 2 chip select, 4 data direction (1 = the CPU drives it), 5 clock direction, 6 select direction

commands.0: status 1 (1 byte: bit 0 reset, 1 24-hour mode, 2-3 general purpose, 4-5 interrupt flags, 6 low battery, 7 power on)
commands.1: status 2 (1 byte: interrupt 1 mode, general purpose, alarm 2 enable, test)
commands.2: date and time (7 bytes: year, month, day, weekday, hour, minute, second)

limits: alarms and the interrupt output are stored but never fire; the clock adjustment register has no effect; the command byte is understood in either bit order
